stem: The two outer legs of a steel tower are straight and meet at the top, as shown. The legs are 30 meters apart at ground level. A horizontal platform 40 meters above the ground spans the legs and is 18 meters wide. What is the height, in meters, of the tower? Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
solution: The platform is parallel to the ground, so the small triangle above the platform is similar to the whole triangle formed by the legs and the ground.
Let \(h\) be the height of the tower. The small triangle has base 18 and height \(h - 40\): \(\frac{h - 40}{h} = \frac{18}{30}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 60 is the height of the part of the tower above the platform; the 40 meters below the platform must be added.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This solves \(\frac{40}{h} = \frac{18}{30}\), but 40 is the height below the platform, not the height of the small triangle.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This adds the 40 meters a second time: the 100-meter height already includes the part below the platform.

verify:
h=symbols('h')
ans=solve(Eq((h-40)/h,Rational(18,30)),h)[0]
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==100
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
assert value(choices['C'])==solve(Eq(40/h,Rational(18,30)),h)[0]
